## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect, which is small and easily overlooked, and more by the woolly galls it produces on live oaks. In Florida, it is associated with live oak and related oaks, especially Quercus virginiana and Quercus geminata, in hammocks, parks, yards, oak woodlands, and other habitats where these host trees occur. The larvae develop inside protective plant galls induced on the oak, feeding within the gall tissue, while the galls themselves can also provide shelter or resources for other small insects after the wasp emerges.
